raw: If Electron's `clipboard.writeBuffer(format, …)` does **not** clear other formats ..., a prior mixed copy's `code/file-list` could shadow a subsequent all-local copy, causing paste of the *previous* selection. Worth an explicit round-trip test across consecutive mixed→local copies.

claim: hasResources and readResources diverge: Paste is enabled when a native format is merely present, but a binary plist from Finder parses to an empty list so the paste no-ops.
raw: **`hasResources` vs `readResources` divergence:** `hasResources` returns true when a native format is merely present (e.g. `NSFilenamesPboardType` from Finder, which is typically a *binary* plist), but `plistToFiles`' XML regex returns `[]` for binary plists — so Paste is enabled yet no-ops.

claim: For an all-remote drag no text/plain is set at all, so dropping a remote file into an in-app text target now inserts nothing — a behavior change.
raw: **DnD text suppression (`dnd.ts:238-248`):** for an all-remote drag, `nativeResources` is empty so no `text/plain` is set at all; dropping a remote file into an in-app text target now inserts nothing (previously inserted the label). Likely intended, but a behavior change.

claim: Proxy readFile buffers whole files in memory across IPC — unbounded for large files on the proxy fallback path.
raw: **Proxy `readFile` buffers whole files in memory** across IPC (`remoteFileSystemProxyServer.ts:263-266`) — unbounded for large files on the proxy fallback path.

claim: Remote file contents are downloaded under cacheHome with default (0755) permissions and cleanup is never awaited, leaving potentially sensitive remote data readable on local disk after the session.
raw: **Impact**: Local information disclosure and data remanence: sensitive remote workspace files are written unencrypted to a persistent local location and can outlive the session; on shared machines they may be readable by other local users.

claim: RemoteFileSystemProxyServer performs no scheme validation of its own, a defense-in-depth gap that becomes an arbitrary-file-read confused deputy if any future caller forwards a file:// URI.
raw: **Impact**: Latent arbitrary-file-read confused deputy across windows if the single upstream check is ever bypassed or a second caller is added; the readFile path additionally skips even the `getProvider` guard the other methods have.

claim: String.fromCharCode(...u16.subarray) spread can throw RangeError on a very large clipboard buffer (caught, returns empty).
raw: `String.fromCharCode(...u16.subarray)` spread can throw `RangeError` on a very large clipboard buffer (caught, returns `[]`)

claim: Pasting clipboard-supplied file:// paths allows user-gesture-driven reads of arbitrary local paths.
raw: pasting clipboard-supplied `file://` paths allows user-gesture-driven reads of arbitrary local paths (inherent to file-manager paste, untrusted-clipboard already acknowledged).

claim: The catch fallback produces a duplicated clipboard (temp copy plus original remote URI for each succeeded file), and the broad catch collapses unrelated error classes into one branch.
raw: `result` now contains **both** the local temp copy *and* the original remote URI for every resource that succeeded before the failure. ... Pasting will produce **two copies of the same file** ..., with zero indication to the user that anything went wrong

claim: The download failure is invisible to the user — only a logService.warn, no notification, status bar message, or Explorer UI signal.
raw: The *only* signal on failure is `this.logService.warn('Failed to download remote files for clipboard', error)`. There is no `notificationService` toast, no status bar message, nothing surfaced through the Explorer UI

claim: cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir has a literal empty catch block that swallows every del failure with no logging, so copies of remote content can accumulate on disk undetected.
raw: This is a textbook empty catch block — no logging at any level, not even `trace`. Per the project's own stated standard ("Never use empty catch blocks... always log errors"), this is a direct violation, not just a stylistic nit.

claim: dispose() calls the async cleanup without awaiting it, so cleanup is not guaranteed to complete before disposal proceeds.
raw: *(Minor, same block)*: `dispose()` at `explorerService.ts:567-570` calls `this.cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir()` without awaiting it — a fire-and-forget promise in `dispose()`. ... cleanup is not guaranteed to run to completion before disposal proceeds.

claim: The register catch swallows the real registration failure so activateProvider resolves normally and callers see a misleading generic ENOPRO 'no provider found' error instead of the root cause.
raw: Because this catch swallows the error and never rethrows, the joined promise **always resolves**, so `Promises.settled` never learns registration failed, and `activateProvider` returns normally. ... it's the **wrong** error — it discards the actual root cause

claim: getRendererChannel can hang forever instead of erroring when no connected client matches, unlike the fail-fast NodeRemoteResourceRouter, and this is reachable during window startup/session restore.
raw: In that window, `RemoteFileSystemProxyMainHandler.call` never throws `"No window found"` (a window *was* found) — it just hangs on `targetChannel.call(command, arg)` forever. No error, no log, no timeout — a paste/DND operation that just spins with no feedback

claim: The three new clipboard parsers log nothing at all in their catch blocks, and plistToFiles' catch is near-dead code that would only ever hide a programmer bug.
raw: **none of the three new methods log anything, even at `trace` level** ... A regression here (e.g., "paste from Finder stopped working after an OS update changed the plist format slightly") would be indistinguishable, from logs alone, from "the user just didn't have anything on the clipboard."

claim: No test exercises the partial-failure duplication path, the empty-catch cleanup path, or the window-known-but-channel-not-registered hang.
raw: No test in the diff (`remoteFileSystemProxy.test.ts:391-468`) exercises the partial-failure duplication path, the empty-catch cleanup path, or the "window known but channel not yet registered" hang — all three are currently unguarded by any regression test.

claim: Partial download failure produces duplicate clipboard entries because the catch re-adds all remote resources including those already pushed as temp targets.
raw: The `catch` then unconditionally pushes **all** original `remoteResources` (including #1 and #2 again), so the returned array contains both the successfully-downloaded temp copy and the original remote URI for the same logical file.

claim: One malformed entry in a text/uri-list payload makes URI.parse throw inside the shared try/catch, discarding every valid entry and silently returning an empty list.
raw: a single bad/unparseable line (e.g. from a non-VS-Code producer writing malformed `text/uri-list` content) causes the exception to propagate out of `.map()`, and the catch then discards every entry — including otherwise-valid file URIs in the same paste — silently returning `[]` with no diagnostic.

claim: dispose() fires the async cleanup without awaiting or catching it — a floating promise, so disposal completes before the deletion I/O finishes.
raw: `cleanupRemoteClipboardTempDir()` is `async` and performs `fileService.del(...)`, but `dispose()` is synchronous and doesn't await or attach a continuation. This is a floating promise — disposal completes ... before the actual deletion I/O finishes.

claim: fileNameWToFile assumes a 2-byte-aligned buffer offset; a RangeError from misalignment is silently swallowed so Windows file-clipboard paste no-ops with no indication.
raw: Constructing a `Uint16Array` view over an existing `ArrayBuffer` at `buffer.buffer.byteOffset` throws a `RangeError` if that offset isn't a multiple of 2. The surrounding `try { } catch { // do not trust clipboard data }` swallows this without any log

claim: The renderer-side proxy server does not itself restrict operations to vscode-remote URIs; the guardrail lives only in the main-process handler.
raw: The renderer-side `RemoteFileSystemProxyServer` channel itself will happily `stat`/`readdir`/`readFile` any scheme the local `fileService` has a provider for, including `file://`. ... the guardrail lives in a different file than the capability it protects

claim: Clipboard resource order is not preserved when mixing local and remote resources — a silent behavior change from the previous single-line implementation.
raw: If the original selection interleaves local and remote items (e.g. `[remoteA, localB, remoteC]`), the returned/clipboard-written order becomes `[localB, remoteA-temp, remoteC-temp]` instead of preserving the original selection order.

claim: The Uint16Array comment conflates JS string encoding with output byte order; the property that matters is endianness, not char encoding.
raw: `// Uint16Array naturally uses the platform's char encoding (UTF-16).` The code itself is correct for the little-endian platforms Windows actually runs on, but the comment's phrasing ("platform's char encoding") is a bit misleading

claim: Schemas is used in dnd.ts with no visible import in the shown diff hunk — flagged as a cannot-verify-from-diff note rather than an assertion.
raw: The diff hunk for this file doesn't include an import line for `Schemas`; since the import section of the file is outside the shown hunk, this may already be imported elsewhere in the file ..., so this is flagged only as a low-confidence "cannot verify from diff" note
